headline: DevOps Engineer | Cloud Engineer | Linux System Administrator
summary: DevOps Engineer trained through the NTI Cloud DevOps Accelerator, with hands-on experience in AWS (EC2, VPC, IAM), Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD with Jenkins and GitHub Actions. Built end-to-end cloud-native projects from infrastructure provisioning and GitOps delivery to security and monitoring, plus a RHEL Linux administration lab, with a focus on automation, security, and scalable system design.

bullets.text: Delivered two end-to-end pipelines for a 3-service application on EKS, one with Jenkins and Ansible and one with GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD GitOps.

Built the final project, an end-to-end pipeline on AWS that provisions infrastructure with Terraform and Ansible, builds and scans images with Jenkins, SonarQube and Trivy, and deploys to EKS with Helm, monitored with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki.

bullets.label: Platform & Security
bullets.text: Five Python/FastAPI banking microservices and an NGINX frontend on EKS, built for financial correctness (fencing tokens, row-lock ordering). Versioned Terraform modules deploy through GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD App-of-Apps, secured with default-deny NetworkPolicies, Istio mTLS, Gateway API and External Secrets Operator (IRSA).

bullets.label: Delivery, Streaming & Reliability
bullets.text: Trivy-scanned, Cosign-signed images are promoted by GitOps PRs and released as Argo Rollouts canaries gated on Prometheus metrics. Strimzi Kafka (KRaft, TLS/SCRAM, ACLs, dead-letter queue) carries events; Pytest concurrency tests, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki observability, and a disaster recovery drill rebuilt the cluster in 23 min 50 s with Multi-AZ RDS.

bullets.label: Infrastructure & Access
bullets.text: Enterprise-style RHEL environment on EC2 (VPN gateway, control, identity, utility and per-team workstations) in private subnets behind a NAT gateway, built with modular Terraform; reachable only through a WireGuard VPN with per-team ranges, firewalld and default-deny security groups.

bullets.label: Automation & Operations
bullets.text: Idempotent Ansible roles (EC2 dynamic inventory) handle SSH hardening, SELinux, firewalld, chrony and fleet patching; Bash scripts rebuild and test the lab, with tickets, runbooks and incident reports documenting changes.

Jenkins multi-branch pipelines for containerized apps on EKS with SonarQube and Trivy quality gates, on Terraform-provisioned infrastructure configured by Ansible; Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki cover metrics and logs.

Serverless CI/CD for a 3-service app on EKS: GitHub Actions authenticates through OIDC with no stored AWS keys, secrets sync from AWS Secrets Manager, and ArgoCD keeps the cluster in sync with Git; monitored with Prometheus and Grafana.

paragraphs: I am applying for the DevOps Engineer role at Nilecode Systems. I build cloud platforms as code and prove they recover, from Terraform and EKS to GitOps delivery. I completed the NTI Cloud DevOps Accelerator and a DevOps internship at iVolve Technologies, where I delivered two end-to-end pipelines on EKS.

Your posting asks for CI/CD with Jenkins or GitHub Actions and for Terraform on AWS. On the Nexora banking platform, I built secretless GitHub Actions pipelines that assume AWS IAM roles through OIDC, with versioned Terraform modules for the VPC, EKS and RDS MySQL. ArgoCD releases the API gateway as a 10%, 50% and 100% canary that aborts if the Prometheus 5xx error rate exceeds 5%. I also built Jenkins multi-branch pipelines on EKS with a Shared Library and SonarQube and Trivy quality gates. For Linux, I am building a RHEL 10 lab on AWS (in progress) with modular Terraform, Ansible and OpenSCAP CIS Level 1 hardening.

I like owning the path from a commit to a running, observable service, and making that path safe enough that a release can be rolled back by a metric instead of a person. In Nexora's disaster recovery drill, I deleted the EKS cluster and rebuilt it to a healthy application in 23 minutes 50 seconds through Terraform and ArgoCD. I would welcome a conversation about bringing that approach to Nilecode Systems.

email_body:
Hello,

I am applying for the DevOps Engineer role at Nilecode Systems in Cairo.
My CV and cover letter are attached.
My background covers AWS, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins, GitHub Actions and Linux administration.
I would be glad to discuss the role.
why_this_role: This role matches the work I did on Nexora and at iVolve: Terraform on AWS, Docker and Kubernetes on EKS, and CI/CD with GitHub Actions and Jenkins, plus RHEL administration in my Linux lab.
